name: Wolf Moon (Full Moon)
description: The first full moon of 2026 — known as the Wolf Moon in the northern hemisphere.

name: Quadrantids — peak
description: Zenithal rate up to 120 meteors per hour. Radiant: star Beta Boötis.

name: Snow Moon (Full Moon)
description: February full moon.

name: Worm Moon (Full Moon)
description: The first full moon of spring.

name: Spring equinox
description: Day and night are nearly equal in length.

name: Pink Moon (Full Moon)
description: The Pink Moon.

name: Lyrids — peak
description: Up to 18 meteors per hour. Radiant: star Vega.

name: Flower Moon (Full Moon)
description: The May full moon.

name: Eta Aquariids — peak
description: Meteor shower from Halley's Comet. Up to 50 per hour.

name: New Moon
description: Darkest sky of the month — best for deep-sky observing.

name: Strawberry Moon (Full Moon)
description: The June full moon (Strawberry Moon).

name: Jupiter–Moon conjunction
description: The Moon passes close to Jupiter in the evening sky.

name: Summer solstice
description: The longest day of the year.

name: Perseids — peak
description: The most popular meteor shower. Up to 100 meteors per hour.

name: Partial solar eclipse
description: Total solar eclipse over North Atlantic. Partial over Europe.

name: Partial lunar eclipse
description: Partial lunar eclipse visible from Europe.

name: Autumn equinox
description: Day and night are nearly equal in length.

name: Draconids
description: Sometimes an intense shower. Radiant: constellation Draco.

name: Orionids
description: Meteor shower from Halley's Comet. Up to 20 per hour.

name: Leonids
description: Up to 15 meteors per hour, with potential for storms.

name: Geminids — peak
description: One of the most beautiful meteor showers. Up to 120 per hour.

name: Winter solstice
description: The shortest day of the year.

name: Ursids
description: A smaller shower, up to 10 meteors per hour.
